The Hartley Transform is a real-valued integral transform that maps a real input function to a real spectrum, serving as an alternative to the complex Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) for real-valued data [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the Hartley Transform is a real-valued integral transform mapping real input to a real spectrum and serves as an alternative to the complex DFT for real-valued data. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Given a real function h(t) its Hartley transform will be real too.' It provides the integral definition $H(f) = h(t)(cos ft + sin ft)dt$, confirming it is a real-valued integral transform. It also details the conversion between Hartley and Fourier transforms, implying its utility as an alternative representation for real data, and discusses the Discrete Hartley Transform in section 2.3.2, linking it to the context of the DFT.
